newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Clarke says no rate meddling prior to UK election.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says no rate meddling prior to UK election.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Friday he would not "start messing around" with monetary policy prior to the British general election.

"I think commentators should leave the elections out of the count. The truth is they are very used historically, I agree, to looking around the word and seeing that politicians start messing around with monetary policy in the run-up to an election," Clarke told Reuters Financial Television in Hong Kong.
"I'm not doing that and I don't think there are any political pressures to do that in the U.K."
Clarke said economics not politics would decide rate direction.
"If the economic evidence made me want to change rates, I'd be able to sell it. I wouldn't cost me any votes and I suspect my opponents would agree with me."
Clarke said he did not have a target for the exchange rate and said his goal for monetary policy was to see stability.
"It (sterling strength) is one factor, but only one factor," he said.
"Strength of sterling certainly is going to have a deflationary effect and its full efect has yet to work through."
Clarke said he sees no evidence that British exporters are suffering from the effects of a strong sterling.
